items.title: CAR T-Cell Therapy BPX-601 for Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1 trial tests BPX-601, a CAR T-cell therapy made from a patient's own immune cells, to treat advanced prostate cancer that has returned or spread. The study aims to identify the best dose and understand side effects. CAR T-cells are engineered to recognize and destroy cancer cells.

items.title: Platform Study of Multiple Anti-Cancer Agents in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1b/2 trial evaluates the safety, dosing, and preliminary effectiveness of multiple new anti-cancer drugs in patients with metastatic prostate cancer. The platform design allows testing of several different treatments. Results will help determine which agents should advance to larger studies.

items.title: Mevrometostat Plus Enzalutamide vs Enzalutamide Alone for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares the combination of investigational drug mevrometostat with enzalutamide versus enzalutamide alone in men with metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer who have not previously received hormone therapy or chemotherapy. The study tests whether adding mevrometostat improves outcomes.

items.title: Docetaxel Plus SX-682 for Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial tests SX-682, a new drug that targets immune cells in tumors, combined with docetaxel chemotherapy for advanced prostate cancer that has spread or returned. The study enrolls patients with head and neck cancers, salivary gland cancers, and prostate cancer. SX-682 is taken as a pill.

items.title: Fasting or Ketone Supplementation Trial in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This study tests whether 7 days of water-only fasting, a ketogenic very low-calorie diet, or ketone supplements is safe and feasible for prostate cancer patients. Animal studies suggest fasting may help immune cells kill cancer cells through metabolic changes. Results will guide future studies on incorporating fasting into treatment plans.

items.title: Cabozantinib Plus Lu-177-PSMA-617 Dose-Finding Study
items.summary: This phase 1b trial tests different doses of cabozantinib combined with Lu-177-PSMA radioligand therapy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study will identify the safest and most effective dose combination for future testing. The trial is currently suspended.

items.title: Ifinatamab Deruxtecan vs Chemotherapy for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares ifinatamab deruxtecan (I-DXd), a new antibody-drug conjugate, to standard chemotherapy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The main goal is to determine if I-DXd helps patients live longer overall and delays cancer progression compared to chemotherapy.

items.title: XL092 Phase 2 Trial for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 study evaluates how well XL092, an oral tablet taken once daily, treats metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer after 16 weeks. Researchers will assess cancer response, safety, and tolerability. Patients return for regular clinic visits during treatment.

items.title: Darolutamide Plus Hormone Therapy After Surgery for High-Risk Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares adding darolutamide to androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) versus ADT alone after surgery for high-risk prostate cancer. Darolutamide blocks testosterone effects in tumor cells. The study tests whether the combination prevents cancer from returning or progressing better than ADT alone.

items.title: HLD-0915 Safety and Efficacy Study in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial assesses the safety and effectiveness of HLD-0915 in patients with metastatic prostate cancer who have progressed on prior therapies. The study will also evaluate HLD-0915 in additional prostate cancer patient populations to understand its potential benefit.

items.title: BNT324 vs Docetaxel Chemotherapy for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares BNT324 to standard docetaxel chemotherapy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients previously treated with hormone therapy but not chemotherapy. The study will determine if BNT324 delays cancer progression and extends overall survival better than docetaxel.

items.title: STEAP1 CAR-T Cell Therapy Plus Enzalutamide for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial tests STEAP1 CAR-T cell therapy combined with enzalutamide in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. CAR-T therapy genetically modifies a patient's immune cells to recognize and attack cancer cells expressing STEAP1. The study evaluates safety and effectiveness of this combination immunotherapy approach.

items.title: Luxdegalutamide Plus Lu-177-PSMA Radioligand Therapy in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial evaluates luxdegalutamide (JSB462) at two different doses combined with Lu-177-PSMA-617 radioligand therapy compared to Lu-177-PSMA alone in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Patients must have received prior hormone therapy and 0-2 chemotherapy regimens. The study will select the best dose for phase 3 testing.

items.title: Cabozantinib Plus Immunotherapy for Rare Genitourinary Tumors
items.summary: This phase 2 trial studies cabozantinib combined with nivolumab and ipilimumab immunotherapy in rare genitourinary tumors that have spread. While focused on rare GU cancers, the study may include some prostate cancer subtypes. The combination aims to enhance immune system attack on cancer cells.

items.title: Xaluritamig Safety Study in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1 trial determines the safety profile of xaluritamig in adults with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Xaluritamig is a novel immunotherapy being tested at a proposed treatment regimen. The study will assess side effects and tolerability.

items.title: Xaluritamig Plus Hormone Therapy for Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1 trial evaluates the safety and tolerability of xaluritamig immunotherapy combined with either darolutamide or abiraterone hormone therapy in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. The study tests whether this combination approach is safe before potential larger trials.

items.title: Inflammation Pathways Drive Treatment Resistance in Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This review discusses how chronic inflammation through NFκB and IL6/JAK/STAT3 pathways reshapes prostate cancer biology and promotes castration-resistant disease. These inflammatory signals work together with androgen receptor signaling to drive tumor survival, spread, and treatment resistance. Understanding these pathways may identify new treatment targets.

items.title: PSMA DNA Vaccine Enhances Immune Response and PD-1 Blockade Effectiveness
items.summary: This preclinical study developed a nanoplasmid-based DNA vaccine targeting PSMA, a protein highly expressed in aggressive prostate cancer. The vaccine generated strong immune responses, prevented tumor growth and metastasis in animal models, and enhanced the effectiveness of PD-1 checkpoint inhibitor therapy. This approach may help overcome resistance to immunotherapy in prostate cancer.

items.title: Real-World Use of Genomic Testing in Finnish Cancer Patients
items.source: ESMO real world data and digital oncology
items.summary: This Finnish study reviewed 297 cancer patients who received comprehensive genomic profiling between 2017-2020, including prostate cancer patients. About 65% had actionable genetic alterations that could guide treatment selection. Patients were heavily pretreated, with half having received three or more prior therapies before testing.

items.title: Targeting PI3K/AKT Pathway in PTEN-Deficient Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This article reviews how PTEN loss activates the PI3K/AKT pathway, driving prostate cancer progression and treatment resistance. PTEN deficiency occurs in many advanced prostate cancers and represents a biomarker for selecting patients who may benefit from PI3K/AKT pathway inhibitors. The review discusses current biomarker-guided therapy approaches.

items.title: Machine Learning Model Predicts Survival in Prostate Cancer with Bone Metastases
items.source: The aging male : the official journal of the International Society for the Study of the Aging Male
items.summary: Researchers developed a machine learning model to predict overall survival in prostate cancer patients with bone metastases who did not have surgery. The model identified Gleason score as the most important survival factor, more critical than tumor stage. The model could help clinicians identify high-risk patients needing aggressive early treatment.

items.title: Meta-Analysis of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This meta-analysis of 21 clinical trials including 1,580 patients examined immune checkpoint inhibitor effectiveness in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer without biomarker selection. One-year survival was 63% and two-year survival 39%. Combination therapy with checkpoint inhibitors showed better outcomes than single-agent immunotherapy, though overall response rates remained modest.
